description:
Problem: while develop's red streak is unreverted, the arm gate (scripts/trunk_revert.py arm-gate; #3415, #3433) refuses to arm every PR except the culprit's revert. On 2026-10-24 the right repair was a fix-forward (#3385), and the only way through was an owner ruleset relaxation. Advisor finding F14 adds a second defect: once a later run fails on a newer tip, the genuine causal revert can fail its identity check because the SHA differs (tests/unit/scripts/test_trunk_revert.py:448-504).

Outcome: a narrowly authorized fix-forward path, bound to the PR number, the head SHA and the failing Trunk run. Required checks, oracle-gate, review threads and holds still apply.

Decision gates:
1. Authorization signal. The gate must verify the authorization through the GitHub API, including the actor's identity: for example a label applied by the owner, or an owner comment naming the PR, head and failing run, similar to the stand-in format. Branch names and commit-message claims are never authorization. If no API-verifiable owner signal is available, stop and ask the owner which one to use.
2. Scope. The exemption covers arming only; it never bypasses required checks or holds.
3. Causal revert identity. Match the genuine revert by culprit PR number, not by the newest failing tip's SHA. Show that a later failing tip no longer blocks it.

Item guardrails: no unrestricted --force flag; no ruleset edits; no change to merge-authority holds; no change to who may revert.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests.
